career_paths.title: Android Developer
career_paths.description: Master modern Android development with Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, and Clean Architecture.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Activity Lifecycle
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Understand how Activities are created and destroyed.
knowledge_nuggets.content: The Activity lifecycle consists of states like onCreate, onStart, onResume, onPause, onStop, and onDestroy. Managing these correctly prevents memory leaks and ensures a smooth user experience when switching apps.

quizzes.text: Which method is called first when an Activity is created?
quizzes.explanation: onCreate() is the first callback and where you initialize your activity.

quizzes.text: Which state is an Activity in when it is partially obscured but still visible?
quizzes.explanation: onPause() is called when the activity is no longer in the foreground but still visible.

knowledge_nuggets.title: ViewModel Pattern
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Manage UI data in a lifecycle-aware way.
knowledge_nuggets.content: ViewModels store and manage UI-related data so it survives configuration changes like screen rotations. They decouple your UI logic from the Activity/Fragment lifecycle.

quizzes.text: Does a ViewModel survive a screen rotation?
quizzes.explanation: Yes, ViewModels are specifically designed to survive configuration changes.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Hilt Dependency Injection
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Standardize DI in your Android apps.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Hilt is a DI library for Android that reduces the boilerplate of manual dependency injection. It is built on top of Dagger and provides a standard way to incorporate DI into your app.

quizzes.text: Which annotation is used to mark the Application class for Hilt?
quizzes.explanation: @HiltAndroidApp triggers Hilt's code generation.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Retrofit Networking
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: Connect your app to the internet.
knowledge_nuggets.content: Retrofit is a type-safe HTTP client for Android. it turns your HTTP API into a Java/Kotlin interface, making network requests easy to handle and test.

quizzes.text: Which library is often used with Retrofit for JSON parsing?
quizzes.explanation: Converter factories like Gson or Kotlinx Serialization handle JSON mapping.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Room Database
knowledge_nuggets.content: Room provides an abstraction layer over SQLite to allow fluent database access while harnessing the full power of SQLite. It handles boilerplate and provides compile-time checks.

quizzes.text: What does a DAO stand for in Room?
quizzes.explanation: DAOs define the methods that access the database.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Jetpack Navigation
knowledge_nuggets.content: The Navigation component helps you implement navigation, from simple button clicks to complex patterns, such as app bars and the navigation drawer.

quizzes.text: What is the new recommended way to define routes in Navigation 2.8.0+?
quizzes.explanation: Navigation now supports type-safe routes using Kotlin Serialization.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Compose State
knowledge_nuggets.content: In Compose, state is any value that can change over time. When state updates, Compose automatically re-executes the functions (recomposition) to reflect the changes in the UI.

quizzes.text: Which function is used to keep state across recompositions?
quizzes.explanation: remember stores an object in the composition.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Kotlin Coroutines
knowledge_nuggets.content: Coroutines allow you to write asynchronous code as if it were synchronous. They are highly efficient and provide built-in cancellation and structured concurrency.

quizzes.text: What keyword is used to define a coroutine-friendly function?
quizzes.explanation: suspend functions can be paused and resumed without blocking.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Kotlin Flow
knowledge_nuggets.content: Flow is a stream of data that can be computed asynchronously. It is similar to an Iterator but uses suspend functions for asynchronous values.

quizzes.text: Which Flow type is best for representing UI state?
quizzes.explanation: StateFlow is a state-holder observable flow that emits the current and new state updates.

knowledge_nuggets.title: WorkManager
knowledge_nuggets.content: WorkManager is the recommended solution for persistent work. It handles tasks that need to run even if the app exits or the device restarts, like data syncing.

quizzes.text: Is WorkManager suitable for immediate, high-priority tasks?
options: Only if the app is open
quizzes.explanation: WorkManager is for tasks that can wait but must eventually run.

knowledge_nuggets.title: DataStore
knowledge_nuggets.short_description: The modern way to store preferences.
knowledge_nuggets.content: DataStore is a data storage solution that allows you to store key-value pairs or typed objects with protocol buffers. It uses Coroutines and Flow to store data asynchronously.

quizzes.text: What does DataStore replace?
quizzes.explanation: DataStore is the replacement for SharedPreferences.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Clean Architecture
knowledge_nuggets.content: Clean Architecture divides the app into layers (Data, Domain, Presentation). The Domain layer contains business logic and is independent of UI or external libraries.

quizzes.text: Which layer should NOT know about Android frameworks?
quizzes.explanation: The Domain layer should be pure Kotlin/Java with no dependencies on the platform.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Solid Principles - SRP
knowledge_nuggets.content: A class should have only one reason to change. This means a class should only perform one primary task, making it easier to maintain and test.

quizzes.text: What happens if you violate SRP?
quizzes.explanation: Violating SRP leads to massive classes that are hard to debug.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Testing - JUnit
knowledge_nuggets.content: JUnit is the standard testing framework for Android. Unit tests verify the smallest parts of your app in isolation, usually the business logic in your Domain or ViewModels.

quizzes.text: Where do unit tests usually reside in the project structure?
quizzes.explanation: Local unit tests run on the JVM and go into the 'test' folder.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Advanced R8/Proguard
knowledge_nuggets.content: R8 is the built-in tool that shrinks, desugars, and obfuscates your code. Obfuscation renames classes and members to make reverse engineering more difficult.

quizzes.text: What is the primary goal of obfuscation?
options: Make code harder to read for humans
quizzes.explanation: Obfuscation protects intellectual property by making reverse engineering difficult.

career_paths.title: UI/UX Designer
career_paths.description: Learn to design beautiful, user-centered mobile and web applications.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Color Theory
knowledge_nuggets.content: Color theory involves the color wheel, harmony, and the psychological impact of colors. Warm colors evoke energy, while cool colors suggest calmness.

quizzes.text: Which color is often associated with trust and professionalism?
quizzes.explanation: Blue is widely used in corporate and financial apps to build trust.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Grid Systems
knowledge_nuggets.content: Grids provide structure and consistency. A standard 8dp or 4dp grid helps in aligning elements and ensures that the layout looks professional across all screens.

quizzes.text: Why use an 8dp grid system?
options: Consistency and divisible by most screen sizes
quizzes.explanation: An 8dp grid makes scaling across different screen densities easier.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Wireframing
knowledge_nuggets.content: Wireframes are low-fidelity sketches that focus on layout and functionality without getting distracted by colors or typography. They are the 'skeleton' of your UI.

quizzes.text: What is the main purpose of a wireframe?
quizzes.explanation: Wireframes define where elements go and how the user moves between screens.

knowledge_nuggets.title: User Research
knowledge_nuggets.content: User research involves interviews, surveys, and testing to understand user needs. Designing without research is like shooting in the dark.

quizzes.text: What is a 'User Persona'?
options: A fictional character representing a user segment
quizzes.explanation: Personas help teams empathize with the target audience.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Accessibility (A11y)
knowledge_nuggets.content: Accessibility ensures that people with disabilities can use your app. This includes screen reader support, large touch targets, and high contrast ratios.

quizzes.text: What is the minimum recommended touch target size?
quizzes.explanation: 48x48dp is the minimum size for comfortable tapping.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Contrast Ratio
knowledge_nuggets.content: The contrast ratio measures the difference in brightness between text and background. WCAG 2.1 requires at least 4.5:1 for normal text.

quizzes.text: Which ratio is better for accessibility?
quizzes.explanation: Higher contrast makes text easier to read for users with low vision.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Visual Hierarchy
knowledge_nuggets.content: Visual hierarchy uses size, color, and weight to show importance. It helps users scan a page quickly and find the information they need.

quizzes.text: How do you create visual hierarchy?
quizzes.explanation: Contrast in size and weight tells the user what to read first.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Fitts's Law
knowledge_nuggets.content: Fitts's Law states that the time to move to a target depends on the target's size and distance. In UI, place frequently used buttons close and make them large.

quizzes.text: According to Fitts's Law, what makes a target easier to hit?
quizzes.explanation: Large, nearby buttons are fastest to interact with.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Micro-interactions
knowledge_nuggets.content: Micro-interactions are subtle animations that confirm a user's action. Example: A heart icon that pops when liked or a loading bar that moves.

quizzes.text: What do micro-interactions provide?
quizzes.explanation: They make the app feel responsive and human-centric.

knowledge_nuggets.title: Design Systems
knowledge_nuggets.content: A design system is a collection of reusable components, guided by clear standards, that can be assembled together to build any number of applications.

quizzes.text: What is the main benefit of a design system?
quizzes.explanation: It ensures consistency and speed across large products.
